observed_text:
The registered NSK example links Smearing 7 to Smearing 5: the convex rollers in Smearing 7 belong to the same spherical roller bearing shown in Smearing 5, so the bearing type is inherited from that earlier example [EV-I01-002]. For Smearing 7, NSK reports smearing of the rolling surfaces on those convex rollers and attributes that example to poor lubrication [EV-I01-002]. This is the manufacturer's case statement, not a project observation; the general smearing context (oil-film rupture and/or sliding, with possible causes such as high speed and light load, sudden acceleration/deceleration, improper lubricant, or water entry) does not establish a sample root cause or any product/dose [EV-I01-002]. The caller-assigned rolling_element category does not establish the same damage or cause in the CWRU bearing: the source is a spherical roller bearing rather than a CWRU deep-groove ball bearing, and the rolling-element classification does not prove smearing or a lubrication cause [EV-I01-002]. The scenario's poor-lubrication spherical-roller-smearing assumption is an independently specified teaching assumption, not an observation or classifier inference.

Evidence limitations:
The NSK source concerns a spherical roller bearing, not the CWRU deep-groove ball bearing; no transfer validation to CWRU artificial defects or aviation equipment is provided [EV-I01-002].
The rolling-surface smearing and poor lubrication are the manufacturer's reported example, not project observations, and the rolling_element category does not prove smearing or a lubrication cause [EV-I01-002].
No specific lubricant, quantity, or acceptance limit is established, and the scenario assumption is a teaching assumption rather than a source-proven sample fact [EV-I01-002].
No model-specific thresholds, actual device records, or aviation/reuse authorization are supplied in the allowed context.
